blocks.content: NITI Aayog works with the spirit of cooperative federalism, recognizing that strong states make a strong nation.

rows: Had power to allocate funds to states & ministries
Advises only; fund allocation power lies with Finance Ministry
Passive role via National Development Council
Serves as an advisory policy think tank

items: NITI Aayog is an extra-constitutional, non-statutory body created via a Cabinet resolution, just like the former Planning Commission.
Remember that NITI Aayog DOES NOT possess fund allocation powers; this responsibility rests with the Union Finance Ministry.
The Governing Council of NITI Aayog comprises Chief Ministers of all States and Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: NITI Aayog was established on January 1, 2015, replacing the 65-year-old Planning Commission.
Unlike the Planning Commission, NITI Aayog acts purely as an advisory think tank and does not allocate funds to states.
NITI Aayog operates on a bottom-up approach to policy planning, whereas the Planning Commission followed a top-down model.
The Prime Minister of India serves as the Chairperson of NITI Aayog, supported by a Vice-Chairperson and a CEO.
Financial allocation authority previously held by the Planning Commission was transferred to the Ministry of Finance.
